data.long_meaning: Refers to a person belonging to a single lineage or dynasty. The name Ekalavansh is derived from the words 'eka' meaning 'one' and 'lavansh' meaning 'lineage'. This name holds a significant place in Indian mythology, particularly in the epic Mahabharata. The name Ekalavansh carries the meaning “Single Lineage” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekalavansh usually hope their child will grow to embody single lineage and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Ekalavansh was the name of the royal dynasty to which the great hero Arjuna belonged. The name symbolizes the pride and honor associated with the prestigious lineage. In Indian culture, the concept of a strong and united royal family has been deeply embedded and emphasized. Ekalavansh represented the unified force and unity among the members of the Kuru dynasty, emphasizing the idea of unity and brotherhood among the kin. Furthermore, it was believed that the blessings of their lineage's sacred ancestors bestowed divine strength, courage, and wisdom upon its members.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Ekalavansh holds symbolism for remaining steadfast, not letting distractions divert one’s focus from their duty and dedication towards their lineage, ancestors, and the Divine. The name brings to the fore the inner desire to stay devoted to the path of righteousness, upholding the values of the heritage and ancestors. This can manifest as staying true to one's gurus, deities, and spiritual practices, as well as being committed to living in accordance with one's dharma.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ekalavansh: The One Lineage. Symbolizing the unified spirit of being part of a single ancestry, rooted in the eternal wisdom and truth of our ancestors. Spiritually, it signifies the pursuit of enlightenment through the collective knowledge and experiences of our lineage.

historical_references.reference: Eklavansh was the name of the ruler of the ancient Indian republic of Anga, which is believed to be located in the present-day Indian state of Bihar. He is famous for his unyielding devotion to Lord Shiva and is often referred to as 'Mahadeva' or 'Lord of Gods'. According to Hindu mythology, Eklavansh is said to have renounced his throne and became a wandering ascetic, living in the forest and meditating on Shiva.

The name 'Ekalavansh' is derived from 'Ekla', meaning 'one' and 'van' meaning 'forest' or 'clan'. It is believed that Eklavansh was a revered leader of the Anga republic, who was also known as 'Maharaja' or 'Great King'. He is considered an embodiment of loyalty, bravery, and devotion to Lord Shiva.
